claim: Gerber & Green (2000) found personal canvassing substantially increased voter turnout, direct mail had a small effect, and telephone calls had no effect, in a randomized field experiment of ~30,000 New Haven voters ahead of the November 1998 election.
stance_target: foundational empirical basis for treating door-to-door canvassing as the most effective GOTV/persuasion channel, motivating France's continued reliance on it
scope_conditions: New Haven, Connecticut, USA, November 1998 election
quoted_support: Voter turnout was increased substantially by personal canvassing, slightly by direct mail, and not at all by telephone calls. These findings support our hypothesis that the long-term retrenchment in voter turnout is partly attributable to the decline in face-to-face political mobilization.
